body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{K,\varepsilon}\) under which \(X\) is degenerate, the derivative of the augmented normalized moment map \((S,T_1,\ldots,T_K)\), with \(S=P(A,Z)\) and \(T_u=E\{h_{0,u}(Y)e_Ae_Z^{\mathsf T}\}\), has a right inverse on its observed finite-feature score image whose operator norm is bounded by \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\).  Applying the corrected \(\mathfrak I_0\) recovers centered derivatives, and hence centered scores, for \(\pi\), \(M_A\), \(M_Z\), and \(\Gamma_Y\) under the modal labeling.
body.justification: This finite-dimensional derivative inversion is the mandatory first gate before any measurable conditional-\(X\) or full-density lifting claim.
body.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes prove level uniqueness of discrete factors, while Hu and Schennach prove full-law recovery through operators; neither result states this quantitative right inverse for the finite normalized tensor derivative.
body.consumer: It provides the constant-covariate kill test and the local inverse needed to begin the full tangent-completeness proof.
body.proof_tex:
Use the notation of (1) in the proof of Theorem 1 and consider a derivative \((\dot\pi,\dot A_0,\dot Z_0,\dot\Gamma)\) satisfying the probability normalizations
\[
 \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot\pi=0,
 \qquad \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot A_0=0,
 \qquad \mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\dot Z_0=0. \tag{7}
\]
We first prove injectivity of the derivative.  Suppose \(\dot S=0\) and \(\dot T_u=0\) for every \(u\).  Set
\[
 E_A=A_0^{-1}\dot A_0,\qquad E_Z=Z_0^{-1}\dot Z_0,
 \qquad p_j=\dot\pi_j/\pi_j.
\]
After multiplying \(\dot S=0\) on the left by \(A_0^{-1}\) and on the right by \(Z_0^{-\mathsf T}\), its \((r,s)\) entry for \(r\ne s\) is
\[
 (E_A)_{rs}\pi_s+\pi_r(E_Z)_{sr}=0. \tag{8}
\]
The same transformation of \(\dot T_u=0\), followed by (8), gives
\[
 (E_A)_{rs}\pi_s(\gamma_{us}-\gamma_{ur})=0,
 \qquad u=1,\ldots,K. \tag{9}
\]
Now
\[
 \|\gamma_s-\gamma_r\|_2
 =\|\Gamma_Y(e_s-e_r)\|_2
 \geq\sqrt2\,\varepsilon,
\]
so (9) implies \((E_A)_{rs}=0\), and (8) then implies \((E_Z)_{sr}=0\).  Thus both \(E_A\) and \(E_Z\) are diagonal.  Since \(\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}A_0=\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}\), (7) gives \(\mathbf 1_K^{\mathsf T}E_A=0\), hence \(E_A=0\); similarly \(E_Z=0\).  The diagonal part of \(\dot S=0\) then gives \(p=0\), and the diagonal part of each \(\dot T_u=0\) gives \(\dot\gamma_{ur}=0\).  The derivative is therefore injective on the normalized parameter tangent space.

The entries of \(A_0,Z_0\), and \(\pi\) lie in compact simplices, their least singular values and the entries of \(\pi\) are at least \(\varepsilon\), and \(|\gamma_{uj}|\leq\|h_0\|_\infty\).  On this compact set the derivative matrix is continuous.  The injectivity just proved says its least singular value is positive at every point; compactness makes the infimum positive.  Its reciprocal is bounded by the corrected \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}\), which depends only on \(K,L,\varepsilon\), and the fixed feature envelope \(\|h_0\|_\infty\).  The Moore--Penrose inverse of this finite derivative is therefore the asserted right inverse on its image.  Its entries are Borel functions on the fixed-rank set.  The modal gap keeps the selected permutation locally constant, so the recovered derivatives respect the ordered labeling.  Dividing probability derivatives by their positive factor probabilities on supported atoms, and putting score zero on zero-probability atoms, produces the centered factor scores.
